summaries.demographer: Judith Castillo is a 34-year-old never-married woman living alone in an owned townhouse in Lilburn, Georgia, with no children or cohabiting partner (Q51, Q52, Q58, Q84). She was born in Atlanta, grew up in Gwinnett County, and identifies as White and Hispanic/Latina with Hispanic heritage on her father's side (Q87, Q88, Q89, Q97). She has graduate education, specifically an MBA, and works full time as a salaried financial manager with stable upper-middle-income earnings (Q65, Q72, Q90). Her life-course profile is marked by high educational attainment, homeownership, geographic rootedness in metro Atlanta, and close but nonresident family ties (Q05, Q58).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Judith shows high planning orientation, delayed gratification, and strong financial self-control through automated savings, sinking funds, emergency savings, retirement accounts, and avoidance of credit card debt (Q60, Q61, Q63). She tolerates calculated career risk when upside is tied to human capital, as shown by choosing a difficult finance transformation project and learning VBA and Power BI (Q02). Her consumption choices reveal identity-consistent spending on travel, cooking, concerts, fitness, and professional credentials, while she cuts restaurants and trips when expenses rise (Q56, Q60, Q62). She is risk-aware rather than risk-avoidant, keeping cash buffers while investing long term in index and ESG funds (Q61, Q83).
summaries.political_scientist: Judith is a regular voter who participates in presidential, midterm, and local elections and usually votes early in person (Q23). She identifies as a moderately strong Democrat and center-left pragmatist, with priorities including voting rights, health care, education, climate risk, racial equity, reproductive rights, ESG accountability, and competent administration (Q24, Q95, Q96). Her civic orientation is local and institutional: she cares about county services, school boards, zoning, and implementation, and she volunteers in financial literacy (Q17, Q25). She responded to Black Lives Matter through discussion, one protest, donations, workplace equity review, and support for data transparency and accountability in policing (Q26, Q27, Q29).
summaries.psychologist: Judith presents as conscientious, analytical, achievement-oriented, and socially warm, with a self-concept built around competence, mentorship, integrity, and steadiness under pressure (Q01, Q65, Q109). She regulates stress through yoga, cooking, hiking, puzzles, structured routines, therapy when needed, and direct support from friends and family (Q37, Q43, Q45). Her mild anxiety appears tied to responsibility and perfectionism rather than pervasive dysfunction, as shown by her reaction to a dashboard error and her response of improving controls rather than withdrawing (Q44, Q45). She balances ambition with an explicit concern that work not flatten her relationships, health, or community life (Q50, Q108).
